title: Spain Wins the 48-Team World Cup
place: MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford, New Jersey, United States
text: The largest World Cup ever, with 48 nations, ended in New Jersey with Spain beating Argentina 1-0. Argentina played all of extra time with 10 men, and Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute. Spain had outshot Argentina 20 to 3, but goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez made 12 saves, the most ever in a final. It was Spain's second title, after 2010.

source.name: CBS News: Spain beats Argentina to win 2026 World Cup

title: Darkness Falls Over Spain at Sunset
text: Millions of people in cloudless Spanish towns watched the country's first total solar eclipse in more than a century. In Medinaceli, a Roman-era hilltop town, a language teacher said no photo or video comes close to the real feeling. Totality lasted about a minute near sunset, with temperatures above 35°C. Spain set up about 350 official viewing sites, and many pharmacies ran out of eclipse glasses.

source.name: OPB (AP): Millions crowd cities to see Spain's first total solar eclipse in over a century

title: A Judge From Durban Wins the Peace Prize
text: Navi Pillay, born into a family of Indian Tamil origin under apartheid in Durban, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for promoting peace and international law. She once defended Nelson Mandela and other anti-apartheid activists. Later, as a judge at the Rwanda tribunal, she helped establish that rape could be a crime against humanity and genocide. She also served as UN human rights chief.

source.name: NobelPrize.org: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 press release

title: Asia's Games Return to Japan
place: Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, Nagoya, Aichi, Japan
text: The 20th Asian Games opened in Nagoya, the first hosted by Japan since Hiroshima in 1994. Athletes from 45 nations would compete for 469 gold medals across 43 sports until October 4, with swimming held in Tokyo. The ceremony's theme was "Harmonic Heart Beat", and former hammer thrower Koji Murofushi lit the cauldron together with his father, Shigenobu.

source.name: The Korea Times: Competition begins with celebration of host city's hospitality

title: Lula's Comeback in Brazil's Runoff
text: After losing Brazil's first round on October 4, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, aged 80, won the runoff against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro with over 51 percent and more than 64 million ballots. It gave him a fourth, non-consecutive term. No other modern Brazilian politician had lost the first round and then won the runoff. Bolsonaro did not concede and said he would challenge the result.

source.name: Al Jazeera: Lula holds off far right with victory in Brazil presidential election

title: A Classicist Poet Wins the Nobel
text: Toronto-born poet Anne Carson, 76, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. A professor of classics, she blends poetry and essay with ancient Greek literature; her Trojan Women retells Euripides as a graphic book. She holds Icelandic citizenship and was in Iceland when the news came. Asked by Icelandic broadcaster RUV for her reaction, she called it simply "crazy."

source.name: Al Jazeera: Canadian Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature

title: New Zealand's Knife-Edge Election
text: New Zealanders voted in an election with no clear winner. Labour and National each won just over 29 percent of the party vote, and Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's conservative bloc held 67 of 131 seats, one above a majority, before nearly 400,000 special votes were counted. The Opportunity Party, led by 38-year-old Qiulae Wong, entered Parliament with seven seats. Final results were due November 27.

source.name: OPB (AP): No clear winner in New Zealand election

title: A Sweltering 250th Birthday
place: Independence Hall, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, United States
text: The United States marked 250 years since independence in a heat wave, with Washington's heat index near 115°F. In Philadelphia, fireworks went off around midday near Independence Hall, where the Declaration was adopted. In New York, 43 tall ships paraded past the Statue of Liberty, and at Coney Island Joey Chestnut ate 66 hot dogs in 10 minutes for his 18th win.

source.name: PBS NewsHour (AP): Fireworks, heat, hot dogs and politics as America celebrates its 250th birthday

title: A Mountain Collapse Floods Nepal's Valleys
text: On August 26, a glacial collapse high on the Nepal-China border sent a tsunami-like flood down Nepal's river valleys. Nuwakot district, including Devighat on the Tadi and Trishuli rivers, was among the places hit. Nepal counted over 1,000 deaths within a week, and Al Jazeera later reported more than 1,400 killed. A month on, Nuwakot and Rasuwa were told to stay alert as new monsoon rains came.

source.name: Al Jazeera: Floods and landslides kill at least 56 people in India, 12 in Nepal

source2.name: PBS NewsHour (AP): Nepal's death toll from glacier collapse and flood exceeds 1,000

title: Israel's Election Ends in Deadlock
text: Israel's parliamentary election left neither main bloc with the 61 seats needed to govern. Final official results gave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats and the opposition bloc of Gadi Eisenkot 48. Arab-led parties, including the Joint List and Ra'am, held the balance. Israel's Central Elections Committee said the vote was conducted lawfully, rejecting claims of systematic interference.

title: Yurt Villages for the Nomad Games
text: More than 3,000 competitors from 110 countries came to Kyrgyzstan for the World Nomad Games, with horse riding and archery staged in the Kyrchyn Gorge. Each Kyrgyz region built a village of decorated yurts and nomad dwellings with felt-making, carpet-weaving and food cooked on the spot. Over 150,000 visitors came in the first two days. A Mongolian champion kept his title by crushing 58 animal bones in one minute.

source.name: Euronews: Kyrgyzstan's World Nomad Games continues as new village brings history to life

title: A Nobel for a Telescope Made of Ice
place: IceCube Neutrino Observatory, South Pole, Antarctica
text: Francis Halzen won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for IceCube, a cubic kilometre of South Pole ice fitted with light sensors. He first proposed the idea in 1988. Neutrinos pass through Earth unnoticed, but when one rarely hits an atomic nucleus it makes a flash of light in the clear glacial ice. IceCube, finished in 2011, found neutrinos from far outside our solar system.

source.name: NobelPrize.org: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026 press release

title: Solving the Mirror-Molecule Mystery
place: Tokyo University of Science, Tokyo, Japan
text: Living things use only one mirror-image form of molecules like amino acids, a puzzle over a century old. The 2026 Chemistry Nobel went to Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai, a Hiroshima-born professor emeritus at Tokyo University of Science. In 2003 Soai presented a reaction producing only one of two mirror images, something nothing except life itself had achieved before.

source.name: NobelPrize.org: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026 press release

title: Switching Brain Cells On With Light
place: Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Martinsried, Germany
text: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine honoured optogenetics. Peter Hegemann, working at Martinsried's Max Planck institute, and Georg Nagel found channelrhodopsin in a single-celled alga that swims toward light; blue light opens a channel through it. Karl Deisseroth put its gene into rat nerve cells and fired them with light, and by 2007 in living mice. Researchers now use it to map memories and behaviour.

source.name: NobelPrize.org: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 press release

title: Zambia Re-Elects Hichilema
text: Five days after Zambians voted, the electoral commission declared President Hakainde Hichilema the winner of a second five-year term with about 61.4 percent of valid votes. It was his seventh run for the presidency. His rival Brian Mundubile, on his first bid, took about 38 percent and called for an investigation into result forms. EU observers called the vote largely peaceful but said freedoms were limited.

source.name: Al Jazeera: Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema wins second term

title: Eleven Nations Meet by Manila Bay
text: Leaders of the 11-nation ASEAN bloc opened their annual summit at a heavily guarded convention center by Manila Bay. Timor-Leste's prime minister, Xanana Gusmão, stood in the group photo. On the agenda: Myanmar's civil war, South China Sea tensions, energy security and the fallout of distant wars. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. was to hand the rotating chairmanship to Singapore.

source.name: Boston Globe (AP): Southeast Asian leaders open annual summit

title: A Record Storm Hugs Mexico's Coast
text: Category 4 Hurricane Simon, with 140 mph winds, crept along Mexico's Pacific coast with its eye just offshore. Puerto Vallarta closed its waterfront, and Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal towns. Simon pushed the eastern Pacific to a record for accumulated cyclone energy, beating 2018, in a season of 21 named storms fuelled partly by El Niño.

source.name: PBS NewsHour (AP): Hurricane Simon hits Mexico's Pacific coast

source2.name: Al Jazeera: Two deaths reported as Hurricane Simon, storm Rachel batter Mexico's coast

title: Glasgow Closes Its Commonwealth Games
text: Glasgow's Commonwealth Games ended after 11 days with a closing ceremony on August 2. Athletes from 74 nations and territories competed in 215 events across 10 sports and 6 para sports, and 1,168 medals were handed out. More than 630,000 people joined in at venues, city live sites and festival events. The Games were hailed as a "game-changer" for the event's future.

source.name: Glasgow Life: Glasgow 2026 Games ends on a high

title: Taming Booms and Busts Wins a Nobel
place: Stanford University, Stanford, California, United States
text: The 2026 economics prize went to Robert E. Hall of Stanford, born in nearby Palo Alto, and Michael Woodford of Columbia. After the 1970s oil crises, many thought governments should stop trying to smooth booms and recessions. The pair rebuilt economic models on how forward-looking households and businesses behave, and central banks and governments around the world now use such models.

source.name: NobelPrize.org: Prize in Economic Sciences 2026 press release
